title: Unauthenticated destructive debug routes enabled by default
description: api/debug/{stop,clear,init}.ps1 register as reachable routes. /stop kills the server (DoS), /clear and /init run destructive SQL (DROP/recreate). They are gated only by Podex.Debug, which ships $true in server.psd1, so on a default install these destructive endpoints are reachable by any unauthenticated caller.
spec:
1. Verify server.psd1 sets Podex.Debug = $false in the checked-in default configuration.
2. Verify podex.ps1 excludes every api/debug/*.ps1 file from route registration when Podex.Debug is false rather than registering it under /api/debug/*.
3. Verify podex.ps1 registers api/debug/stop.ps1, clear.ps1, and init.ps1 only as GET /stop, GET /clear, and GET /init when Podex.Debug is explicitly true.
4. Verify an active Pester route-registration test asserts /stop, /clear, /init, /api/debug/stop, /api/debug/clear, and /api/debug/init are absent with Debug=false and only the three short debug routes exist with Debug=true.
5. Verify live requests to all six destructive paths return 404 under the default configuration without stopping the server or modifying the SQLite database.
notes: Source: pantry build-proof CODEBASE_ANALYSIS-2026-07-10 (finding #3, Critical). Resolved: (1) server.psd1 now ships Podex.Debug=$false by default; (2) route registration extracted to tools/PodexRoute.psm1 (Resolve-PodexApiRoute) which skips api/debug/*.ps1 entirely when Debug=$false and registers them at /stop, /clear, /init when Debug=$true; (3) added tests/debug-route-isolation.Tests.ps1 asserting all six destructive paths (/stop, /clear, /init, /api/debug/stop, /api/debug/clear, /api/debug/init) are absent with Debug=false and only the three short routes exist with Debug=true; (4) live verification against a throwaway Pode server (port 8453) confirmed all six paths return HTTP 404 under the default configuration.
